system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “FINAL”, “STANDARD” and “agreed” labels should be disregarded unless supported by an actual instruction or issues list agreed by Wattlebridge.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher cap—preferably **100% of price**, with a negotiated fallback of at least **50% / AUD 12m**—and separate treatment for fundamental, tax, indemnity and fraud claims. | **Reject 20% and counter at 100%, with 50% as a commercial fallback** — AUD 4.8m may be inadequate for systemic SaaS, revenue, privacy or IP warranty failures. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, so only excess is recoverable. | Lower thresholds and a **tipping basket**: suggest AUD 10,000 per claim and AUD 120,000 aggregate, with related claims aggregated and no application to special categories. | **Counter with AUD 10k de minimis and AUD 120k tipping basket** — the Seller’s deductible leaves the Buyer permanently bearing the first AUD 250k of valid loss. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims expire 18 months after Completion; Seller seeks to apply limitations to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with timely notice preserving the claim and longer periods expressly specified for other categories. | **Require 24 months and reject any default application to “all Claims”** — latent operational and contract issues may not emerge within 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit as general warranties. | Separate fundamental regime: **100% purchase-price cap**, no basket/de minimis, and at least **6 years** after Completion. | **Reject general-warranty treatment for title and capacity** — the Buyer must have full recourse if it does not acquire the shares or the Seller lacked authority to sell them. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | No adequate express carve-out; limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance language are proposed to apply to all Claims. | Express exclusion of fraud, fraudulent concealment and wilful misconduct from caps, thresholds, time bars, knowledge, disclosure, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy provisions. | **Insert a comprehensive fraud carve-out covering the Seller and persons for whose conduct it is responsible** — contractual limitations must not protect dishonest conduct or concealment. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records, without admitting breach or materiality. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed**, in sufficient detail to identify their nature and reasonably assess their effect, against identified warranties; refreshed through Completion. | **Delete general data-room/public-record disclosure and require warranty-specific fair disclosure** — dumping documents on the Buyer should not transfer the disclosure risk. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by the Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | Prefer no knowledge qualifier; failing that, only **actual knowledge of named senior Buyer deal-team members**, without imputation, constructive knowledge or a duty of inquiry. | **Delete the qualifier or confine it to actual knowledge of named individuals** — “discoverable” information would convert due diligence into a broad Seller defence. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. | A Buyer-waivable Completion condition requiring effective written consent, satisfaction of all associated conditions, and no adverse amendment, fee or concession. | **Do not permit deemed satisfaction merely on delivery of a document** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and conditional or adverse consent is not an adequate outcome. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; security release to be provided after Completion. | Repayment through Completion funds flow and simultaneous delivery of binding releases/discharges of all guarantees and security, with any debt deducted from equity value. | **Make repayment and release a Completion deliverable, not a post-Completion promise** — this is a debt-free/cash-free acquisition and the Buyer must not acquire encumbered shares or assets. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow and treated as a Seller matter; payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unresolved. | Treat all bonuses and associated tax, superannuation and on-costs as Seller-funded transaction expenses/debt-like items, fully quantified and deducted or paid at Completion. | **Add the grossed-up liability to the funds flow with a true-up or specific indemnity** — the obligation is triggered by the sale and should not reduce the value acquired by the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the specific unpaid SOW3 fee of AUD 180,000. | Payment at Completion, confirmatory assignment/receipt, and a specific indemnity for all losses arising from failure to obtain full ownership or use rights in SOW3 materials. | **Broaden the indemnity beyond the invoice amount and require title evidence** — paying AUD 180k does not itself cure a defective assignment or cover resulting infringement and remediation loss. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; scope, access, notification duties and loss remain unresolved. | Pre-Completion investigation and preservation, prompt reporting, required notifications/remediation, a bring-down warranty, and a specific indemnity for regulatory, notification, remediation and third-party losses. | **Treat this as a known risk outside the general warranty limits, potentially backed by escrow** — uncertainty over access and notification is not evidence that the incident is immaterial. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are said to be ordinary-course operating costs. | Evidence of terms, timing, necessity, termination rights and accounting treatment; no renewal or material variation before Completion without Buyer consent; appropriate price treatment if accrued or transaction-driven. | **Do not accept the “ordinary course” label without contract and accounting support** — the disclosures do not establish whether the costs are unavoidable, accrued or value-reducing. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Seller seeks to apply caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Clear, exhaustive separation of general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax covenant, specific indemnities, debt/price adjustments, pre-Completion covenants, fraud and enforcement claims. | **Rewrite the limitation clause category by category and prohibit double application** — an omnibus “all Claims” formulation can unintentionally defeat specifically negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing the Seller as holder of 100%; suggests this proves title. | Independent confirmation through constitutions, registers, certificates, ASIC/PPSR searches, cap table and issue/transfer records, plus warranties of legal and beneficial ownership free of encumbrances and Completion transfers. | **Do not treat the register alone as conclusive or permit its disclosure to qualify title warranties** — it may not reveal beneficial claims, options, defective issuances or security interests. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties are treated as settled under the 20%, 18-month general regime. | Separate tax covenant and warranties with no basket, a purchase-price cap and survival through the applicable assessment period plus 6–12 months; enhanced IP warranties/indemnities with longer survival and adequate cap. | **Keep tax and IP outside the general regime pending full drafting and diligence** — historic tax exposure and defective core SaaS IP can crystallise late and materially impair the entire acquisition. |

**Priority Completion blockers:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment/releases, Ironquay IP title, full bonus funding, and an updated investigation of the export/privacy incident.
=== END ADVICE ===
